title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
read_level: partial (full main text, Appendices C, E and parts of F read; Appendices A, B, D, G, H, I skimmed)
metadata_mismatch: Paper byline gives abbreviated names ("Farias, T.S., Porto, C.M., Fonseca, M. S., Carpio, N. A. C., De Oliveira, A. A., Villas-Boas, C. J"); metadata spells fourth author's surname "Carpi", paper has "Carpio". Full given names taken from metadata.
why_wsp: Frozen GPT-6 Astra writes complete parameter vectors for fixed variational quantum circuits from OpenQASM 3 and Pauli-Hamiltonian descriptions, optionally refining with energy feedback; framed as motivated by WSP but the target is a quantum circuit, not a neural network.
domain: variational quantum eigensolver (molecular H4, LiH; random and parent Hamiltonians); blind quantum circuit interpretation
target: parameterized quantum circuits: UCCSD (8-qubit, 26 parameters for H4), hardware-efficient ansatz with p = 3n(L+1) parameters for n in {4,8,12}
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: all parameters written: "Each inference produces one complete numerical parameter vector, rather than an individual coordinate update." (Sec II.A)

headline_results.claim: Random Hamiltonians: LMO worse than Adam
headline_results.quote: Adam progressively reduces the energy gap through iterative optimization, whereas the LMO generally produces parameter configurations with larger gaps and shows limited improvement over subsequent rounds.
headline_results.where: Sec III.A.2; Fig 5 (figure only for values)

headline_results.quote: the LMO reaches the target accuracy in 40 of 45 instances (88.9%) for r = 1 and 37 of 45 instances (82.2%) for r = 2.
Across both families, the best observed proposals reach the target accuracy in 80 of 90 instances (88.9%).
All four LMO runs achieve energy errors near numerical precision within the first few evaluations.

headline_results.claim: Direct energy predictions violate spectral bound
headline_results.quote: Direct LLM energy prediction frequently produces estimates below the true ground-state energy, violating the spectral lower bound.

headline_results.claim: Blind circuit interpretation: algorithm ID vs output
headline_results.quote: Across these 30 interpretations, the model predicts the correct most-likely measurement outcome in 29 cases (96.7%).
The model correctly identifies all 15 algorithms in the logical representation, compared with 11 of 15 in the native representation and 12 of 15 in the obfuscated representation.
rounding the proposed angles to Clifford-compatible values causes all 90 first proposals to exceed the success threshold

cost.claim: Only Hamiltonian evaluations counted; LLM inference cost not reported
cost.quote: The comparison concerns Hamiltonian expectation-value evaluations rather than the total computational cost of LLM inference.

baselines_and_controls: Adam with parameter-shift gradients (LR searched over {1, 0.1, 0.01}); direct LLM energy prediction; blind vs physics-aware prompts; logical/native/obfuscated circuit representations
runs_and_variance: 3 independent runs per prompt configuration for H4 and LiH (1 blind run for LiH); 5 instances per configuration for random and parent Hamiltonians; variance shown in figures only. Quote: "performance varies across independent runs." (Sec III.A.1)
robustness_of_edits: Distorted non-planar H4 geometry tested (Appendix D): "the quality of LMO-generated parameters varies substantially across independent runs"; noiseless simulation only
verification: variational principle: evaluated circuit energy is an upper bound on ground-state energy; exact diagonalization references; circuit equivalence verified numerically before interpretation
memorization_vs_reasoning: Authors state results "do not establish that the model performs general quantum-mechanical reasoning. Its performance may depend on patterns encountered during pretraining"; Bernstein-Vazirani outputs predicted correctly even when algorithm not identified; LMO solutions often differ from hidden planted angles.
limitations_stated: No general computational advantage; LLM inference cost not counted; feedback effect not isolated from extra proposals; structured Hamiltonians may admit specialized classical solutions; few instances per algorithm; explanations not shown to be faithful.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (ref [24])
Kundu, Ghosh, Honavar, Weight-space programming of variational quantum circuits arXiv:2611.11537 (concurrent)
notes_for_survey: Extends the WSP framing to VQC parameters; success depends strongly on problem structure (parent Hamiltonians near-solved, random Hamiltonians not). Contrasts unverifiable direct energy predictions with variationally verifiable parameter proposals.
